question: Can the convolutional U-Net backbone of latent diffusion models be replaced by a standard transformer, and how does sample quality scale with transformer forward-pass Gflops?
hypothesis: The U-Net inductive bias is not crucial to diffusion model performance, and transformers (ViT-style) inherit favourable scaling with compute.
contributions: Diffusion Transformers (DiT): a ViT-based backbone operating on latent patches for latent diffusion models
Study of four conditioning block designs (in-context, cross-attention, adaLN, adaLN-Zero)
Scaling analysis of model size and patch size via Gflops vs FID, with state-of-the-art class-conditional ImageNet 256x256 and 512x512 FID

method.summary: Latent diffusion models (frozen off-the-shelf Stable Diffusion VAE) whose denoiser is a ViT-style transformer on 2x2/4x4/8x8 patches of the latent, conditioned on timestep and class via adaLN-Zero. 12 configs (S/B/L/XL x patch 8/4/2) are trained on class-conditional ImageNet and compared on FID against Gflops; DiT-XL/2 is trained to 7M steps (256) and 3M (512).

datasets.name: ImageNet
datasets.preprocessing: only horizontal flips as augmentation; images encoded by VAE to 32x32x4 (256px) or 64x64x4 (512px) latents

models.name: DiT-S
models.init_from: ViT-standard init; final linear layer zero-initialised

models.name: DiT-XL
models.context: inferred: 256 tokens at 256px p=2 (T=(I/p)^2 with I=32); 1024 tokens at 512px p=2

models.name: Stable Diffusion VAE (ft-EMA / ft-MSE / original LDM f8 decoder)
ADM, ADM-U, ADM-G, LDM-4, LDM-8, CDM, BigGAN-deep, StyleGAN-XL

training.objective: L_simple (MSE on noise) for epsilon, full variational lower bound L for learned covariance Sigma (Nichol and Dhariwal); class label dropped to learned null embedding for classifier-free guidance (dropout probability not stated)
training.steps: 400K for the 12-model sweep; DiT-XL/2 256x256 7M (2352K and 7000K rows in Table 4); DiT-XL/2 512x512 3M
training.compute: estimated as model Gflops x batch size x training steps x 3
training.wall_clock: DiT-XL/2 trains at roughly 5.7 iterations/second on a TPU v3-256 pod with global batch size 256

other.hyperparameter_source: retained almost entirely from ADM; not tuned (lr, schedules, Adam betas, weight decay)
other.timestep_embedding: 256-d frequency embedding then two-layer MLP with SiLU
other.adaLN_output: linear layer to 4x (adaLN) or 6x (adaLN-Zero) hidden size
other.diffusion: t_max=1000, linear variance schedule 1e-4 to 2e-2, ADM covariance parameterisation

inference.decoding: DDPM sampling, 250 steps for reported FID-50K; classifier-free guidance
inference.samples: 50K samples for FID-50K (10K for FID-10K in sampling-steps study); single run, no seeds stated

parameters.cfg_scale_table2_3: 1.25 and 1.50 (guidance on first 3 of 4 latent channels only); 4.0/6.0 used for qualitative figs
parameters.cfg_channels: first three of four latent channels; 3-channel scale 1+x approx 4-channel scale 1+0.75x

metrics.name: FID-50K
metrics.definition: Frechet Inception Distance on 50K samples, computed with ADM's TensorFlow evaluation suite

metrics.name: Precision/Recall
metrics.definition: Kynkaanniemi et al. 2019; 1000 real samples at 512px for consistency with ADM

eval.protocol: FID without guidance in scaling study unless stated; ft-MSE decoder for scaling analysis, ft-EMA decoder for Tables 2-3; single run, no variance reported

results.setup: DiT-XL/2-G cfg=1.50, 7M steps, 250 DDPM steps, ft-EMA decoder, ImageNet 256x256

results.note: Table 4 lists 3000K steps for the 3M model; StyleGAN-XL FID 2.41 at 512 is lower than DiT 3.04 in Table 3 though text says DiT beats prior diffusion models

results.claim: Transformer Gflops are strongly negatively correlated with FID-50K across the 12 DiT models
results.setup: 12 DiT models (S/B/L/XL x p=8,4,2) at 400K steps, no guidance, Fig 8

results.claim: DiT-XL/2 reaches FID 2.55 when trained only 2.35M steps (similar to ADM)
results.quote: XL/2 still outperforms all prior diffusion models with an FID of 2.55

results.claim: Without guidance DiT-XL/2 at 256x256 gets FID 9.62 vs 10.56 for LDM-4 and 10.94 for ADM
Smaller models with more sampling compute do not catch up: XL/2 at 128 steps beats L/2 at 1000 steps with 5x less sampling compute

results.quote: XL/2 has the better FID-10K (23.7 vs 25.9)

results.claim: adaLN-Zero is the best conditioning block; at 400K iterations its FID is nearly half the in-context model's
results.table: Table 4, row DiT-XL/2 adaLN-Zero 400K, column FID-50K

results.claim: DiT-XL/2 uses far fewer Gflops than ADM at 256x256 (118.6 vs 1120) and at 512 (524.6 vs 1983)
results.setup: per forward pass, DDPM component only, 256x256

results.claim: Cross-attention adds roughly 15% Gflops overhead; in-context adds negligible Gflops
Three-channel guidance at scale 1.5 matches four-channel guidance at scale 1.375 (FID 2.20)
results.setup: DiT-XL/2 256x256 7M steps, guidance on 4 channels, scale 1.375
results.quote: four-channel guidance with a scale of 1.375 gives an FID-50K of 2.20

results.claim: VAE decoder choice changes FID slightly: original LDM decoder gives 2.46 vs 2.27 with ft-EMA
Training is stable without warmup or regularisation: no loss spikes observed

limits: Class-conditional ImageNet only; the text-to-image use (DALL-E 2, Stable Diffusion) is proposed as future work, not tested.
Scaling is shown only to 675M parameters / 118.6 Gflops at 256 px; authors say future work should scale to larger models and token counts.
Single runs with no seeds or variance reported; ImageNet size, split and licence not stated.
Gflops vs FID correlation is measured at 400K steps only; Table 3 shows StyleGAN-XL still has lower FID at 512x512 (2.41 vs 3.04).
Hyperparameters were not tuned (borrowed from ADM), so the U-Net comparison may favour either side; guidance applied to only 3 of 4 channels.
Parameters and Gflops exclude the 84M-parameter VAE; the pipeline depends on a frozen pre-trained VAE.
